`builder.py` works on a checkout with tools, and the words follow. `Plane` becomes `Tools`, and every `world` in names, parameters, keys, docstrings, comments, messages and the usage line becomes `checkout`: the usage line reads `builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`, the numbers key `world` becomes `checkout`, `world_head` becomes `head` in the numbers and the function that computes it becomes `head()`. In the role text `a world` becomes `a checkout` and nothing else in it changes. The checkout must be a git checkout: a directory without `.git` is a usage error, exit 2, before any run directory exists, so the branches that record `not a git checkout` and a null head go, and `head` is always a commit. `plans` leaves `HIDDEN`. `test_builder.py` already uses the new names; the tests whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour and the rest of the suite must stay green.

The documents follow after the build, by the attended agent: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the seed template and the seeds say checkout and tools; the notes of v0.1 to v0.4 keep their words as history, and one sentence in `AGENTS.md` maps the old words to the new.

From the review of the first build: the module docstring lists `diff.patch (what the run left in the checkout; absent when it left nothing)` and `record_diff`'s docstring says the patch is absent when the run left nothing, since that is what the build made true and the tests pin; the comment above `HIDDEN` no longer speaks of planning; a directory whose `.git` is not git's, a stray file, is refused as `not a git checkout`, and a checkout with no commit as `the checkout has no commit`; the joined patch is bound once; the two docstrings that said `the five functions of the tools` and `Not a function of the tools` say `the five tools` and `not one of the tools`.

From the review of the second build: a checkout is the root of its own repository, which `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run in it must name, and git runs with `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` removed from its environment, so a subdirectory of a repository, with or without a `.git` of its own, and a directory the environment points elsewhere are refused as `not a git checkout`, while a worktree, whose `.git` is a file, is a checkout; a git that cannot run before the run is a usage error naming git, never a traceback; the comment above the guard explains both its halves; the module docstring says `reachable only through five tools` and no longer names a version.

From the review of the third build: the two diffs of `record_diff` run with `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv`, so neither the environment, nor the configuration, nor a `.gitattributes` in the checkout can replace the patch with a program's output; a git that ran and failed before the run directory exists, whichever call it was, is a usage error carrying git's own message, exit 2, and a good checkout is not called `not a git checkout` for a failure of git's.

From the review of the fourth build: the diffs of `record_diff` end their options with `--`, so a file the run names like an option or a revision, `-x.txt` or `HEAD`, still yields the patch and the numbers; a directory is refused as `not a git checkout` only when git itself says `not a git repository` or `invalid gitfile format`, and any other failure of git's, at whichever call before the run, is a usage error carrying git's words in the same shape, with no probe; `.gitattributes` and `.gitignore` are protected from write and edit at any depth, since a filter or an ignore rule the model wrote would change what git records of the run.

2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a checkout until its tests pass.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"

6	The checkout is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through five tools:
7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the checkout and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the checkout's tests in a container with no network and the
9	checkout mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key

12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the checkout, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl

318	class Sandbox:
319	    """Where the checkout's tests run: a container, no network, the checkout mounted read-only.
320	
321	    The only place that knows about Docker. The image is the checkout's own locked dependencies,
322	    built once per (uv.lock, check.Dockerfile) pair and reused by every run afterwards.
323	    """
324	
325	    @staticmethod
326	    def image(checkout: Path) -> str:
327	        """The image name for this checkout: what it locks and how it is built, hashed."""
328	        h = hashlib.sha256((checkout / "uv.lock").read_bytes() + (checkout / "check.Dockerfile").read_bytes())
329	        return f"factory-check:{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"
330	
331	    @staticmethod
332	    def ensure_image(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> str:
333	        """Build the image if it is not there yet; the build is the one step with network."""
334	        name = Sandbox.image(checkout)
335	        seen = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", name], capture_output=True)
336	        if seen.returncode == 0:
337	            return name
338	        built = subprocess.run(
339	            # -f absolute: docker resolves a relative -f against the caller's directory, and the
340	            # factory never runs from inside the checkout.
341	            ["docker", "build", "-f", str(checkout / "check.Dockerfile"), "-t", name, str(checkout)],
342	            capture_output=True,
343	            timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT,
344	        )
345	        (run_dir / "image-build.log").write_bytes(built.stdout + built.stderr)
346	        if built.returncode != 0:
347	            raise RuntimeError(f"docker build failed (exit {built.returncode}); see image-build.log")

9	an empty cell, and `head` reads `head` and, before v0.5, `world_head`. A record without
10	`numbers.json` is a row with its stamp and goal alone. Nothing is written. Any argument is a
11	usage error on stderr, exit 2.
12	"""

15	
16	import json
17	import sys
18	from pathlib import Path
19	from typing import Any
20	
21	RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "runs"  # the factory's record, beside this file
22	
23	COLUMNS = (
24	    "stamp", "head", "stopped", "check", "requests", "tool_calls", "lists", "reads", "writes", "edits",
25	    "checks", "input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "output_tokens", "reasoning_tokens", "cost_usd",
26	    "seconds", "files_changed", "insertions", "deletions", "goal",
27	)  # fmt: skip

29	
30	def usage_error(reason: str = "") -> int:
31	    print("usage: runs.py", file=sys.stderr)
32	    if reason:
33	        print(reason, file=sys.stderr)
34	    return 2
35	
36	
37	def _first_line(path: Path) -> str:
38	    """The first line of `path`, tabs as spaces; empty when the file or its first line is absent."""
39	    try:
40	        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
41	    except OSError:
42	        return ""
43	    return lines[0].replace("\t", " ") if lines else ""
44	
45	
46	def _numbers(record: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
47	    """The record's `numbers.json` as a mapping; empty when it is absent or unreadable."""
48	    try:
49	        data = json.loads((record / "numbers.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
50	    except (OSError, ValueError):
51	        return {}
52	    return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
53	
54	
55	def _field(value: Any) -> str:
56	    """One cell: a string as it is, anything else as JSON prints it; a tab or newline becomes a space."""
57	    text = value if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value)
58	    return text.replace("\t", " ").replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ")

62	    keys = ("head", "world_head") if column == "head" else (column,)
63	    for key in keys:  # v0.5 renamed the field; older records carry the checkout as world_head

73	    records = sorted(p for p in base.iterdir() if p.is_dir()) if base.is_dir() else []

81	                _cell(numbers, column)
82	                for column in COLUMNS
83	            )
